title: Pluggable block store: selectable Kubo/S3/filesystem backend
description:
The block storage backend is currently hardcoded to Kubo via KuboHttpClient. Different deployments need different backends: Kubo for operators already running IPFS, S3 for cloud deployments, filesystem for single-node or dev use.

This epic covers the selection layer only — not the S3 or filesystem implementations themselves.

## What needs doing

- Add a [backend] config section to both transit and reader configs with a type discriminator field (kubo, s3, filesystem, sqlite, lmdb, rados, git_sha256)
- Add backend-specific sub-sections ([backend.kubo], [backend.s3], [backend.filesystem]) parsed via serde enum
- Write a factory function in each crate that constructs Arc<dyn IpfsStore> / Arc<dyn IpfsBlockStore> from config, dispatching to the appropriate implementation
- Factor any shared codec/error-mapping helpers into core so all backends can reuse them
- Retire the current top-level [ipfs] config section (replace with [backend]); provide a migration note in the runbook
- IPNS publisher wiring: Kubo supports it; S3 uses a manifest writer; other backends disable it — the factory should return an Option<IpnsStrategy> alongside the store

## IpfsStore trait: delete method

Add a delete method to IpfsStore and IpfsBlockStore:

```rust
async fn delete(&self, cid: &Cid) -> Result<DeletionOutcome, IpfsError>;

pub enum DeletionOutcome {
    /// Article has been removed immediately. get() will return NotFound.
    Immediate,
    /// Article has been marked for deletion. It remains readable via get()
    /// until the backend's own reclaim process runs (Kubo GC, S3 lifecycle rule, git gc).
    /// The caller must not assume the article is gone until get() returns NotFound.
    Deferred { readable_for_approx_secs: Option<u64> },
}
```

Backend-specific delete semantics:
- Kubo: calls pin/rm. DeletionOutcome::Deferred — article remains in Kubo's block store and is readable until `ipfs repo gc` runs (operator-controlled, potentially hours or days).
- S3: two modes — see S3 epic. DeletionOutcome::Deferred when using lifecycle tagging; DeletionOutcome::Immediate when using explicit DeleteObject.
- Filesystem: unlinks the file. DeletionOutcome::Immediate.
- SQLite: DELETE FROM blocks. DeletionOutcome::Immediate.
- LMDB: txn.delete. DeletionOutcome::Immediate.
- Ceph RADOS: rados_remove. DeletionOutcome::Immediate.
- Git SHA-256: removes from CID→git_sha256 index only. DeletionOutcome::Deferred — git object remains in the object store and is readable until git gc --prune runs.

## GC contract

The GC runner must never assume an article is inaccessible after calling delete. It must handle DeletionOutcome::Deferred correctly:
- Log the outcome (article marked for deletion, readable until backend reclaims)
- The retention report records both the delete call and the expected reclaim window
- Clients issuing ARTICLE or BODY commands for a deferred-deleted article receive a normal response (not 430 No Such Article) until get() actually returns NotFound

## Acceptance criteria
- Single config change switches backend at runtime
- Kubo path is regression-free (all existing tests pass unchanged)
- S3 and filesystem paths compile and fail fast with a clear error if their epic is not yet merged (stub implementations returning Err('not yet implemented') are acceptable as placeholders)
- delete() returns DeletionOutcome::Deferred for Kubo; get() on the same CID still returns data before Kubo GC runs
- delete() returns DeletionOutcome::Immediate for filesystem/SQLite/LMDB; get() returns NotFound immediately after
